messages:
maya: quick sync — i'm proposing we fold the console 'view-proxy' into a single render-control service instead of the current 3-way proxy + adapter stack. wrote a short follow-up doc (link) but main reasons: simpler routing, consistent caching keys, and easier canarying for model/query-level SLOs.

kishan: curious on perf numbers — do we expect lower p50/p95 for small dashboards or is this mainly operational simplification? :thinking_face:

maya: early perf runs (dev cluster): small panel p50 ~ -9ms, p95 ~ -4ms, p99 roughly same. CPU on render nodes up ~6% due to slightly larger monolith, but overall host count falls because we eliminate cross-process hop.

joanne: RBAC question: how will tenant scoping and folder-level perms map? view-proxy currently enforced per-request with its own cache. we can't accidentally widen reads.

maya: good call. plan is: render-control will be a control-plane-aware service — every request carries the console token and a resolved permission set (short-lived JWT from auth-gateway). caching keys include tenant_id + resolved-perm-hash so we never serve cached results across different permission sets.

kishan: how do we migrate existing caches? the keys differ so warm-up cost might spike.

maya: migration strategy: 1) v1 handle both codepaths behind feature flag; 2) gradually switch a small % of tenants (canary by org id) to render-control, keep view-proxy as fallback; 3) run a passive compare mode (serve from new but also hit old) for 2 weeks; 4) cutover, then evict old caches.

alex: telemetry/alerts: we need token-level cost breakdown + per-tenant latency SLOs. can we reuse existing per-route traces?

maya: yes — plan is augment traces with a `render_path` tag and preserve token_id. console telemetry team already agreed to capture token-level tokenized cost. we'll add a per-tenant dashboard and a regression alert if p95 increases >10% for 30m.

joanne: rollback story? if we see permission regressions we need fast fail-to-proxy option.

kishan: implementation idea: implement a runtime policy that if any auth mismatch is detected we immediately route the request back to view-proxy for that req id and mark a metric. that avoids full service rollback.

maya: yep — fallback routing in the edge with a `prefer_proxy` tag. also plan a canary watchdog that auto-turns the flag off if errors cross threshold.

alex: one more: cost modelling — monolith uses more memory per node. we should run a capacity estimate and update billing forecasts before wide rollout.

maya: already on it — i'll post numbers tomorrow. TL;DR: expected net infra cost neutral to slightly positive for first 30 days then ~12% savings after cache consolidation.

kishan: LGTM on the approach. can you add a follow-up checklist for infra, console, and telemetry teams?

maya: yes — will drop a checklist in the doc and create a short PR template for canary toggles. assigning owners in doc.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: render-control/v1 canary started on cluster-dev-3 (build 2026.03.21-rc5) :rocket:

joanne: :eyes: i'll run a small permission audit against the canary orgs tomorrow and share results.

maya: thanks — appreciate the quick reviews. I'll open the feature-flag PR and add a migration runbook later today.
